overview: Hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan interviewed Medford School Committee member Mea Quinn Mustone regarding district governance, equity, teacher contract negotiations, and community involvement. Mustone also announced that she would not seek re-election following her fourth term ending in 2023.

items.title: Introductions and Local Background
items.summary: Co-host Chelli Keshavan and guest Mea Mustone introduced themselves and discussed their favorite local Medford restaurants.

items.title: Initial Campaign for School Committee
items.summary: Mustone shared the background of her first campaign in 2015, which was driven by the goal of securing full-time paraprofessionals in kindergarten classrooms.

items.title: School Committee Roles and Parent Communication
items.summary: Mustone explained the committee's newly codified policy handbook, Open Meeting Law limitations, and how parents can direct inquiries between school administration and committee members.

items.title: District Representation and Regional Vocational Programs
items.summary: Mustone noted the lack of representation from certain elementary school neighborhoods on the at-large committee and described vocational partnerships that enroll students from Everett.

items.title: District Policy and Curriculum Representation
items.summary: Mustone discussed the committee's responsibilities for hiring the superintendent, approving the budget, and setting district policy to drive equity in classrooms.

items.title: Teacher Contract Negotiations
items.summary: Mustone clarified that negotiations occur between the administration and the Medford Teachers Association before coming to the School Committee for final approval.

items.title: Professional Development for Educators
items.summary: Mustone outlined teacher continuing education requirements, district professional development days, and tuition reimbursement budget constraints.

items.title: Student Support and Committee Turnover
items.summary: Mustone addressed the pandemic's lingering impact on student culture, urged diverse candidates to run for school board, and announced that her current term will be her last.

items.title: Community Events and Ethical Boundaries
items.summary: The participants discussed Medford's upcoming citywide Pride event and how Mustone separates her duties as an elected official from her perspectives as a parent.

items.title: Public Participation and Meeting Access
items.summary: Mustone reviewed public meeting schedules, hybrid Zoom access, subcommittee structures, and the availability of member office hours.
